citation.title: Deep learning-based topological optimization for representing a user-specified design area

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The CNN predicts 32 × 32 topology outputs in 0.07634 s per case versus 0.4393 s for SIMP, an 83% time reduction; the proposed design also has lower reported compliance error on the top 80% of test cases.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: 0.4393 s SIMP time divided by 0.07634 s CNN time per case = 5.756 (Section 4.3/Table 1); article separately states an 83% reduction.
claim.alternatives: Table 2 compares compliance error, volume-fraction error, and design-area satisfaction with Yu's CNN; the proposed model's mean compliance error for the top 80% is 2.75%.

baseline.implementation: Open-source MATLAB topology optimization code (Andreassen et al., 2011)
baseline.solver: SIMP with finite-element analysis; linear solver not stated
baseline.hardware_classical: Same CPU as ML method; CPU model not stated
baseline.hardware_ml: Same CPU as SIMP method; CPU model not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; 370,000 datasets generated and split 296,000/37,000/37,000 for training/validation/test (Section 4.2)
baseline.quality_metric: Mean compliance error, volume-fraction error, and design-area satisfaction rate (Section 4.3, Table 2)
baseline.quality_gap: For the top 80% of test outputs, mean-compliance error is 2.75%; mean volume-fraction error is 9.70%; 99.6% satisfy the design-area threshold of 0.01 (Section 4.3, Table 2 and Fig. 15)

R1.evidence: Section 4.3: time is compared per case on the same CPU, and quality is compared with SIMP, but the compliance result is summarized for the top 80% and the timed runs are not matched by a stated quality threshold.

R2.evidence: Section 4.3 identifies the open-source SIMP implementation and says timings used the same CPU; no text evidence establishes an R2 failure criterion.

R3.evidence: Section 4 reports the 370,000-case dataset size but no data-generation runtime, training time, or amortization for the speed claim.

R4.evidence: Section 4.3 reports compliance and volume errors and a design-area satisfaction rate, and describes occasional disconnected outputs, but does not report their failure rate.

notes: Full text read from arXiv v2. The 83% timing comparison excludes training and data-generation costs. The paper's dataset uses SIMP-generated labels; no release of the article's model code or dataset is stated.
